notes: Single-source synthesis: 0 external research topics; codebase-analysis.json is the substantive Discovery deliverable.

RICE confidence calibration: 'single_sourced' (codebase-only) ⇒ 0.5 across all frames; codebase claims with multiple file citations + verbatim extracts (F-001, F-002, F-003, F-008, F-012, VE-003, VE-004) treated as high-quality single-source ⇒ 0.6.
Per orchestrator note: options enumerated as the GENUINE option space (1–N); no straw-men. Each option marked recommended | rejected with rationale.

The 7-item ADR slate (PRD U-10) is meta-decisions about how decisions get recorded; not framed as standalone decisions here. They are listed under adr_slate_routing at the end and routed to design-composer at Stage 7.
Scope: 12 explicit + 2 discovered = 14 decision frames. Aligns with 'broad' scope (8–15) per decision-framing-knowledge.

decisions.summary: How does `issue-capture-author` agent load `KB-issue-capture` content given that `disable-model-invocation: true` skills are silently dropped from sub-agent `skills:` preloads?
context_claims: F-001 — no existing SKILL.md in this project declares `disable-model-invocation: true`; this run introduces the first two
F-003 — auditing-subagents/references/subagent-spec.md line 110: skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` cannot be preloaded into subagents; SILENT DROP
CP-001 — non-pipeline agent frontmatter precedent (cc-critique) omits `skills:` entirely; structural template
F-013 — intake-intent-clarifier already supports prior_context-style runtime injection; sibling pattern
Issues/issue-capture-mechanism/proposal.md §Cross-references — KB-cc-design Principle 1 (skill-localised knowledge)
PRD FR-3 AC-FR-3-a — KB-issue-capture must refuse description-match auto-load

options.option_name: Runtime Read/Glob in agent body
options.description: issue-capture-author frontmatter omits `skills:` entirely (mirroring cc-critique precedent). The agent body contains an explicit 'Read these reference files' step that uses Read/Glob to load `.claude/skills/KB-issue-capture/SKILL.md` and its `references/*.md` at runtime as part of its procedure.
pros: Sidesteps the silent-drop BLOCKER (F-003) — the constraint cannot be violated because no skills: entry exists
Matches cc-critique structural precedent (CP-001 — closest existing agent template)
auditing-subagents and auditing-cc-configs cross-file checks will pass cleanly (F-003 references the exact check)
Composable with the same pattern for the entry-point `capture-issue` skill if it also gets disable-model-invocation
cons: Reading skill files in the agent body burns context tokens at every spawn (vs. skill-system caching). Mitigation: small KB (~4 reference files)
Discovery of the skill files relies on convention paths in the agent body — refactors that rename `.claude/skills/KB-issue-capture/` must update the agent body string
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Declare KB-issue-capture in skills: anyway (do NOT set disable-model-invocation on the KB)
options.description: Drop the disable-model-invocation constraint on KB-issue-capture so the standard skill-preload mechanism works. The capture-issue entry-point skill retains disable-model-invocation; the KB does not.
pros: Lets the standard skill-loading mechanism work without runtime Read
Smaller agent body
cons: Violates user-confirmed intent: PRD §Product Policy Decisions row 5 names KB-issue-capture's disable-model-invocation as part of Layer 1 of three-layer enforcement
Allows main Claude (and pipeline sub-agents whose descriptions partially match) to auto-load the KB — defeats the non-pollution invariant (FR-13 / Risk #5)
Reduces three-layer enforcement to two-layer; downgrades NFR-4 prompt-injection resistance
options.recommendation: rejected — undoes user-confirmed Layer 1 of FR-3

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (Runtime Read/Glob in agent body). Per F-003 + CP-001 the architecturally clean answer is to omit `skills:` and read at runtime; this is also the only option that preserves all three enforcement layers.
risks: Single-source claim base: F-003 derives from auditing-subagents spec — no executable test in-project demonstrates the silent-drop yet (F-001 — first in project to exercise it)
If the agent body's Read step is itself reachable by prompt-injection, the runtime injection vector is wider than skill-preload; mitigated by NFR-4 (mandatory AskUserQuestion before Write)

decisions.summary: What is the PreToolUse hook's stdin event schema, stdout JSON response shape, exit-code semantics, and error/log destination?
context_claims: PRD U-1 — explicit deferral to design-claude-code
F-002 — NO `.claude/hooks/` directory exists; NO hooks block in settings.json; this IS the first hook in the project
F-007 — auditing-hooks references/ contains 4 files (anti-patterns.md, common-failures.md, hook-spec.md, security-checklist.md); NO examples/good-hook-annotated.md exists
node: kb.cc-platform-extensions — documents hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision = allow|deny|ask; matcher regex; ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}
PRD Assumption 2 — tool_input.subagent_type discrimination is assumed but not demonstrated in this KB
PRD FR-3 AC-FR-3-b — emit permissionDecision: 'ask' with spawn-prompt preview in message field
PRD NFR-2 — fail-open on script error; stderr log
PRD §Risks #5 — first hook in project; no in-project precedent

options.option_name: Bash script + jq, JSON stdin event → JSON stdout permissionDecision
options.description: Hook at `.claude/hooks/intercept-issue-capture-agent.sh`. Reads stdin JSON event (Claude Code-supplied), extracts `tool_input.subagent_type` via jq, branches: if equals 'issue-capture-author' → emit `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"<WHY/WHAT/WHERE-preview>"}}` and exit 0; else emit `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}` and exit 0. Errors (missing jq, malformed stdin) → write `intercept-issue-capture-agent: <reason>` to stderr, emit `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow"}}`, exit 0 (fail-open per NFR-2).
pros: Minimal dependencies (bash + jq, both standard in devcontainer)
Single-file, easy to audit
Sub-100ms wall-clock plausible (jq parse of small JSON ≪ 10ms) — satisfies AC-NFR-1-a
Mirrors sibling auditing-shared scripts' stderr discipline (log_state_transition.py style)
cons: Bash + jq compose is harder to unit-test than Python (D-07 hook test strategy)
Shellcheck-clean is required (cc-critique will flag)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Python script (python3 .claude/hooks/intercept-issue-capture-agent.py)
options.description: Python stdlib-only (json, sys). Same I/O contract as Option 1 but written in Python. Pattern matches auditing-shared/scripts/*.py.
pros: Idiomatic with auditing-shared sibling scripts (CP-002 — argparse, JSON stdin, fail-open default)
Easier unit testing (smoke_test_auditing_shared.py harness style)
Type-safe JSON parsing without jq
cons: Python startup cost (~50-150ms on cold start) puts AC-NFR-1-a's ~100ms target at risk per F-002 (no measured baseline yet)
Adds another permissions.allow entry for python3 invocation (CP-005 shape)
Heavier than bash for a sub-100ms discriminator
options.recommendation: rejected — python3 startup risks AC-NFR-1-a fast-path target on a hook that fires on every Task spawn (NFR-1)

options.option_name: Node script via npx
options.description: Node.js script; uses native JSON parsing.
pros: Native JSON; no jq dependency
cons: Node not currently used in any auditing-shared script — introduces a new runtime
Node startup also ~50-200ms; same fast-path risk as Python
No project precedent (F-002 — first hook; F-007 — no annotated example)
options.recommendation: rejected — introduces new runtime with no project precedent and same startup-cost risk

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (bash + jq). Lowest startup cost (best chance of meeting AC-NFR-1-a's ~100ms target), single-file, stderr discipline matches sibling auditing-shared idiom. Test strategy is D-07's concern.
risks: PRD Assumption 2 (subagent_type lives in tool_input field) is unverified in-project (kb.cc-platform-extensions caveats this); design must verify against live Claude Code platform docs
First hook in the project (F-002) — no precedent to template from; cc-critique pre-merge findings will be load-bearing (PRD U-5)
Hook fires on EVERY Task spawn (NFR-1 blast radius); a regression here breaks ~28 pipeline agents (PRD §Risks #1)

decisions.summary: What is the exact text/structure of the `AskUserQuestion` approval prompt — WHY/WHAT/WHERE rendering and the 4 fixed options (Approve / Approve-with-edits / Change-doctype / Cancel)?
context_claims: PRD U-2 — explicit deferral; lands in KB-issue-capture/references/approval-prompt-rubric.md
PRD FR-1 AC-FR-1-b — exactly one AskUserQuestion with WHY/WHAT/WHERE before any Write
PRD FR-2 AC-FR-2-a — OLD→NEW preview in update-mode
PRD FR-4 AC-FR-4-d — collision re-prompt with 3 options (supersede / rename / cancel)
PRD FR-5 — single AskUserQuestion gates two writes in evolution-transaction case
PRD NFR-4 — agent-body AskUserQuestion is the prompt-injection guard (Layer 2)
intent-clarification.md §What's undecided — 'final wording... lands in approval-prompt-rubric.md at design time'

options.option_name: Structured rubric in approval-prompt-rubric.md with 4 prompt-archetypes
options.description: Author `KB-issue-capture/references/approval-prompt-rubric.md` codifying four archetype prompts: (a) create-mode WHY/WHAT/WHERE with 4 options; (b) update-mode OLD→NEW diff with Approve/Approve-with-edits/Cancel options; (c) filename-collision re-prompt with supersede/rename/cancel; (d) evolution-transaction with both-files preview and single Approve. Each archetype gives canonical question text + the exact AskUserQuestion options array. The agent body cites the rubric at the relevant Step.
pros: Skill-localised (KB-cc-design Principle 1) — the discipline lives in KB-issue-capture, not the agent body
Four archetypes cover the four distinct flows (PRD FR-1, FR-2, NFR-5, FR-5) — no fifth needed
Rubric file is testable: acceptance tests can grep the rendered prompt against expected substrings
Allows wording polish without agent-file edits
cons: Adds a fourth reference file under KB-issue-capture (already had triage-criteria, examples, non-pollution-contract per intent-clarification.md §What's in scope — actually approval-prompt-rubric IS already one of the 4 named files; this is on-plan)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Embed prompt text directly in agent body
options.description: Hard-code the four prompt archetypes inline in `.claude/agents/issue-capture-author.md`.
pros: Single-file source of truth for the agent
No additional reference file
cons: Violates KB-cc-design Principle 1 (skill-localised knowledge) — prompt-rubric is discipline content
Conflicts with intent-clarification.md §What's in scope which names `approval-prompt-rubric.md` as one of the 4 KB-issue-capture reference files
Edits to prompt wording require agent-file edits; harder to iterate
options.recommendation: rejected — violates structural-vs-discipline KB split (one of the 7 ADRs in U-10)

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (rubric file with 4 archetypes). The PRD scope already names approval-prompt-rubric.md as a KB-issue-capture reference file; this design decision finalizes its internal structure.
risks: Prompt wording itself is a UX surface; the recommendation here is structural (where + shape), not the final wording
Single-source: PRD wording for the 4 options is descriptive only — design-claude-code must verify Claude Code's AskUserQuestion 4-option max constraint matches PRD's 4 named options

decisions.summary: Which of the four migrated `Issues/*.md` files demonstrates which doctype in `KB-issue-capture/references/examples.md`, given the doc_type rename from {deferral-register, analysis, proposal} to {issue-register, issue-analysis, issue-proposal}?
context_claims: PRD U-3 — defers worked-example pairing to design-claude-code
F-005 — pre-migration doc_type drift: `deferral-register`, `analysis` (×2), `proposal` do not match PRD FR-7 canonical enum
known_issues[0] — FR-8 migration must back-fill doc_type to canonical enum atomically with git mv
Issues/register-devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals.md — REGISTER precedent (sweep-style tabular: ID/Item/Source/Why deferred/Re-examination trigger/Forgetting risk)
Issues/analysis-per-agent-design-evaluation-gap.md — ANALYSIS precedent (prose + evidence)
Issues/analysis-adr-placement-rootcause.md — ANALYSIS precedent (prose + evidence; second of two analyses)
Issues/proposal-auditing-family-graduation-review.md — PROPOSAL precedent (prose + adoption + proposes_future_feature field)
CP-004 — three doctypes have three distinct body shapes (confirmed)

options.option_name: 1:1 pairing — one example per doctype, picking the strongest exemplar of the two analyses
options.description: examples.md presents exactly 3 worked examples: (1) register doctype → `Issues/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals/register.md` (the only register precedent); (2) analysis doctype → `Issues/per-agent-design-evaluation-gap/analysis.md` (richest evidence-based body, includes the agent-roster-impact-matrix evidence migration per FR-9); (3) proposal doctype → `Issues/auditing-family-graduation-review/proposal.md` (the only proposal precedent in the migration set). Each example shows post-migration frontmatter shape (canonical doc_type, status: open, version: 0.1.0) and explains why this file is shape-defining for its doctype.
pros: Each doctype gets exactly one canonical exemplar — clearest pedagogical mapping
All four migrated files are referenced (register-1, analysis-2 either as primary or 'see also', proposal-1)
The chosen analysis (per-agent-design-evaluation-gap) is also the one that gets FR-9 evidence/ subdirectory treatment — demonstrates that pattern simultaneously
cons: Treats adr-placement-rootcause/analysis as a second-class example (mentioned as 'see also' rather than canonical)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: All-four pairing — two analysis examples shown
options.description: examples.md presents 4 examples: register, analysis-A, analysis-B, proposal. Both analyses get equal treatment.
pros: All four migrated files canonicalized equally
cons: Adds noise; two analysis exemplars dilute the structural signal (CP-004 shows shape is essentially the same)
Bloats examples.md without proportional value
options.recommendation: rejected — three doctypes warrant three exemplars; CP-004 confirms analyses share one shape

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (1:1 pairing). Pick the per-agent-design-evaluation-gap analysis as the canonical analysis exemplar (richest evidence + drives FR-9 evidence/ subdirectory demonstration). Cite adr-placement-rootcause as 'second analysis in the precedent set' without re-rendering it.
risks: Examples.md must use POST-migration paths (Issues/<topic>/<doctype>.md) and POST-rename doc_type values — must be authored AFTER FR-8 migration completes (or paired write in same change-set)

Single-source: codebase analysis enumerates the four files but doesn't independently validate that per-agent-design-evaluation-gap is the 'richest' analysis — design-claude-code should read both before pairing

decisions.summary: For each of the 5 terminal/lifecycle states (`open`, `adopted`, `complete`, `superseded`, `wontfix-with-rationale`), which companion frontmatter fields are MANDATORY vs. OPTIONAL in the validator extension?
context_claims: PRD U-4 — defers per-state required-companion-field set to design-claude-code + design-backend
PRD FR-7 AC-FR-7-c — `status: adopted` without per-state required companion field(s) MUST flag
VE-001 — intra-pipeline 4-state vocabulary: `superseded` requires references to superseding ID (per ADR-0005 in current validator at lines 314-323)
validator_extension_surface.current_per_state_required_companion_fields — superseded already enforces superseded_by
F-009 — pre-migration files all at status:draft; migration back-fills status:open + since: companion
CP-007 — feature_slug universal-required per ADR-0032 Change 4; new templates may set 'pipeline-wide' or '<slug>'
intent-clarification.md Q6 — back-fill status:open + since: on the 4 migrated files
Issues/issue-capture-mechanism/proposal.md frontmatter — uses status:draft + proposes_future_feature: (specific to proposal doctype)

options.option_name: Minimal-mandatory per state, with one back-link field universal across terminal states
options.description:
Companion-field rules:
- `draft`: MANDATORY {id, version, doc_type, feature_slug, generated, generated_by}; OPTIONAL {since, scope, mode, companion_artifacts}.
- `open`: MANDATORY draft set + {since}. (Aligns with migration back-fill per intent-clarification.md Q6.)
- `adopted`: MANDATORY open set + {adopted_by_feature_slug} (back-link to the slug that adopted this issue, e.g., 'issue-capture-mechanism-r1' on its own seed proposal).
- `complete`: MANDATORY open set + {completed_in_feature_slug} (back-link to the slug that closed this).
- `superseded`: MANDATORY open set + {superseded_by_issue_id} (parallel to existing ADR-0005 enforcement for ADRs; VE-001 confirms intra-pipeline vocabulary has the same constraint).
- `wontfix-with-rationale`: MANDATORY open set + {wontfix_rationale} (free-text rationale field).
- Doctype-specific: `issue-proposal` files in `draft` or `open` MAY (advisory, see D-06) carry `proposes_future_feature`; `issue-proposal` files in `adopted` SHOULD carry `proposes_future_feature` (used to derive adopted_by_feature_slug if absent).
- Evolution: `escalates_from` / `escalated_to` are OPTIONAL on any doctype + state; presence required only when FR-5 evolution has occurred.
pros: Mirrors existing ADR-0005 superseded_by enforcement (already in validator at line 314-323) — no new dispatch mechanism needed, just new field names
Each terminal state has exactly one back-link field — symmetric and learnable
Aligns with migration back-fill plan (intent-clarification.md Q6) — status:open + since: passes cleanly
AC-FR-7-c is satisfiable: validator can name the specific missing field per state
Distinguishes from intra-pipeline 4-state (VE-001) via different field NAMES while sharing the back-link DISCIPLINE
cons: Six new field names introduced (since, adopted_by_feature_slug, completed_in_feature_slug, superseded_by_issue_id, wontfix_rationale, plus advisory proposes_future_feature) — onboarding overhead
wontfix_rationale is free-text and structurally unbounded; validator can only check presence, not quality
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Maximal-mandatory: every state requires evidence_paths[] and decision_authority fields
options.description: Adds evidence_paths[] (list of cited files) as MANDATORY on `open` onwards; adds decision_authority (who approved transition) as MANDATORY on terminal states.
pros: More structural rigor; audit trail richer
cons: Bloats frontmatter beyond what the 4 pre-migration files contain — migration would back-fill these speculatively
decision_authority duplicates generated_by intent
Not supported by PRD scope — no FR requires evidence_paths[]
options.recommendation: rejected — scope creep beyond PRD; over-rigid for empirical precedent shape

options.option_name: Minimal: only superseded requires a companion field (mirror current ADR rule exactly)
options.description: Only `superseded` state has a mandatory companion (superseded_by_issue_id). All other states require only the universal frontmatter fields.
pros: Smallest validator-extension surface
Lowest backward-compatibility risk for any post-r1 captures
cons: AC-FR-7-c specifically requires `status: adopted` to flag without per-state companion fields — this option contradicts the AC
Loses audit-trail back-link discipline for adopted/complete/wontfix — defeats the purpose of the 5-state vocabulary
options.recommendation: rejected — directly contradicts AC-FR-7-c

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (minimal-mandatory per state with one back-link field). This is the smallest design that satisfies AC-FR-7-c, mirrors existing ADR-0005 superseded discipline (VE-001 + validator line 314-323), and aligns with the migration back-fill plan.
risks: Single-source: design has no independent validation that adopted_by_feature_slug / completed_in_feature_slug are the right names — design-backend should verify against any other ADR-0032-related conventions before locking the field names
Once mandated, these fields are structurally one-way (relaxing later means existing files become non-validating); deserves the ADR slot already implicit in U-10's 5-state vocabulary ADR

decisions.summary: Is the `proposes_future_feature:` frontmatter field validator-enforced (presence required on `issue-proposal` doctype) or advisory?
context_claims: PRD U-6 — defers to design-backend
F-006 — TWO existing precedents: Issues/proposal-auditing-family-graduation-review.md (suggested-slug format) and Issues/issue-capture-mechanism/proposal.md (fixed-slug format)
Both precedents are on issue-proposal-shaped files (the only doctype where the field is relevant)
Issues/issue-capture-mechanism/proposal.md frontmatter line 11 — the field IS used for the orchestrator's `--raw-request` proposal-seed pattern (FR-11, FR-12)
FR-10 / FR-11 — intake-intent-clarifier detects `doc_type: issue-proposal` (not `proposes_future_feature:`) — so the field is NOT load-bearing for handoff detection
The two precedents use DIFFERENT slug formats (suggested vs. fixed) — no precedent for format enforcement

options.option_name: Advisory: validator notes absence as `info` severity finding on issue-proposal doctype; does not block
options.description: On `doc_type: issue-proposal`, validator checks if `proposes_future_feature:` is present. If absent, emit a single `info`-severity finding ('issue-proposal lacks proposes_future_feature: — consider adding the target feature slug'). Does not flag format; does not block validation. If present, accept any string value.
pros: Honors both existing precedents (F-006) — neither would have been blocked
Adds a forward-pointer hint without coercion
Aligns with sibling-script idiom (CP-002 — observer-only default, info-level findings)
Easy to upgrade later if real-world use shows the field becomes load-bearing
cons: Two info findings on a freshly-migrated proposal file pair (the existing two proposals do carry it, so this is no-op for them)
Info findings can be ignored — discipline is soft
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Mandatory presence on issue-proposal doctype
options.description: On `doc_type: issue-proposal`, validator emits a `major`-severity finding if `proposes_future_feature:` is absent, blocking acceptance.
pros: Stronger discipline; ties proposal doctype to its sole purpose (proposing a future feature)
cons: Both existing precedents pass either way (F-006), so the strictness gains no immediate value
Forces authors to name a future slug at proposal time when they may not yet know it
Conflicts with the design discipline that the field is OPTIONAL on `draft` and SHOULD on `adopted` (D-05 Option 1)
options.recommendation: rejected — strictness without empirical demand; conflicts with D-05's adopted-state shoulder

options.option_name: Not validated at all (ignore the field)
options.description: Validator does not check for the field. It's purely documentary.
pros: Zero validator-extension surface
cons: Loses the forward-pointer signal entirely
Means design-stage tooling cannot rely on validator to surface absence
options.recommendation: rejected — wastes the cheap-to-add info signal

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (advisory info-severity finding). Matches sibling auditing-shared idiom, honors both precedents, adds zero blocking risk.
risks: If future FRs assume `proposes_future_feature:` is reliably present (e.g., auto-derived adopted_by_feature_slug per D-05), this advisory posture leaves a gap; mitigation: D-05 makes adopted_by_feature_slug independently mandatory on adopted state

decisions.summary: What is the test strategy for the new PreToolUse hook script — shellcheck, bash test harness, golden-file dry-run, integration test via real Task spawn, or some combination?
context_claims: PRD U-7 — defers to test-acceptance-author + plan-author
F-002 — first hook in the project; F-007 — no annotated example to template
F-016 — direct-read extraction only; no GitNexus MCP; tooling baseline matches sibling scripts
CP-002 — sibling auditing-shared scripts use stdlib-only + the smoke_test_auditing_shared.py harness pattern
PRD NFR-1 — hook fires ~30-100 spawns/run; latency matters
PRD NFR-2 — fail-open posture must be testable
PRD §Risks #1 — hook regression blocks ~28 pipeline agents; high-blast-radius failure mode

options.option_name: Layered: shellcheck (lint) + golden-file dry-run (unit) + one integration test (smoke)
options.description: Three layers: (a) `shellcheck .claude/hooks/intercept-issue-capture-agent.sh` as a pre-merge lint (zero warnings); (b) golden-file test harness: a Python or bash test script that pipes 4-5 canonical stdin JSON events through the hook and diffs stdout against committed golden files (one each for: issue-capture-author spawn → ask, non-issue spawn → allow, malformed JSON → allow + stderr, missing field → allow + stderr, empty stdin → allow + stderr); (c) one integration smoke test that invokes `/capture-issue dummy` end-to-end during acceptance phase and verifies the AskUserQuestion prompt appears. The unit-layer harness lives at `.claude/hooks/test_intercept_issue_capture_agent.sh` (or .py) mirroring smoke_test_auditing_shared.py.
pros: Three layers map cleanly to NFR-1 (lint catches syntax), NFR-2 (golden-file covers fail-open), AC-FR-3-b/c (integration covers the real-spawn path)
Golden-file diff is the fastest unit-test pattern for stdin/stdout scripts
shellcheck enforces bash discipline at zero runtime cost
Integration test (one only) avoids the cost of spawning Claude Code repeatedly in CI
cons: Three distinct test mechanisms — slightly heavier than a single-layer choice
Golden files need to be regenerated when the JSON event schema changes (mitigated: D-02 locks the schema)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: shellcheck only
options.description: Only static lint; no runtime test.
pros: Smallest test surface
cons: Does not exercise fail-open (NFR-2) or the discriminator logic
Hook regressions land in production
options.recommendation: rejected — does not cover NFR-2 or AC-FR-3-b/c behavior

options.option_name: Integration test only (real /capture-issue invocation)
options.description: Skip unit tests; rely on full integration test in acceptance phase.
pros: Tests the real path
cons: Cannot test malformed-stdin / fail-open branch without a way to inject malformed events
Slow feedback loop (must spawn Claude Code)
Cannot run in pre-merge CI gates without Claude Code itself in the loop
options.recommendation: rejected — fail-open branch (NFR-2) is essentially untestable from outside Claude Code

options.option_name: bats-style bash test harness
options.description: Bash-specific test framework (bats-core).
pros: Bash-idiomatic
cons: Introduces a new external dependency (bats) — not currently used anywhere in the project
Golden-file diff (Option 1's middle layer) achieves the same coverage with no new dependency
options.recommendation: rejected — new dependency without proportional benefit

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (shellcheck + golden-file + one integration smoke). Maps to NFR coverage cleanly, uses no new dependencies, sub-100ms unit-test loop.
risks: Golden-file format is tied to D-02's stdin/stdout schema; schema changes invalidate goldens

The integration smoke requires a working Claude Code session — gating it behind 'manual acceptance' rather than CI is acceptable per recipe-feature-pipeline §Hard exclusions (no automated gate beyond the 6 human gates)

decisions.summary: How does `/capture-issue --update <path>` detect a no-op (idempotency) — content-diff, frontmatter-state-diff, file-hash, or some other mechanism?
context_claims: PRD U-8 — defers to design-claude-code
PRD NFR-3 + AC-NFR-3-a — re-running with empty diff is a no-op, no prompt, no write
PRD FR-2 — update-mode reads file, drafts proposed transition, presents OLD→NEW preview
FR-5 evolution case — only escalated_to: appended to older file (frontmatter-only mutation)
Audit-trail discipline (NFR-6) — terminal-state files never deleted; supersession via frontmatter only

options.option_name: Frontmatter-state-diff: compare proposed-new-frontmatter to current-frontmatter; empty diff ⇒ no-op
options.description: Update-mode flow: (a) Read file at <path>; (b) parse current frontmatter into dict; (c) draft proposed new frontmatter (apply transition: new status value + companion-field additions per D-05); (d) compute diff between current and proposed frontmatter dicts; (e) IF diff is empty (no key added/removed/changed), THEN report 'no change — file already at proposed state' to user, exit without AskUserQuestion or Write; ELSE present OLD→NEW preview in AskUserQuestion. Body content is not compared (per FR-5 audit-trail discipline, body is not mutated by status transitions).
pros: Frontmatter-only diff matches the actual mutation surface (status transitions touch frontmatter only; FR-5 evolution touches only the escalated_to: field)
No false-positives from body whitespace differences or line-ending variations
Cheap to compute (small dict comparison)
Symmetric: a user re-running --update with the same target state correctly reports no-op
Naturally extends to FR-5 transactional case (both files' frontmatter diffs computed independently; if both empty, no-op)
cons: If a future update needs to modify body (out of current PRD scope), this diff would miss it (acceptable; PRD does not require body-mutation in update-mode)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: File-hash equality
options.description: Compute SHA of the proposed file (frontmatter + body re-serialized) and compare to current file's SHA.
pros: Most strict — any byte difference triggers a write
cons: Whitespace/line-ending differences in YAML re-serialization can produce false positives even when the LOGICAL state is unchanged
Requires a deterministic frontmatter serializer; the validator's hand-rolled parser (F-008) doesn't have a canonical writer
Overengineered for the actual mutation surface
options.recommendation: rejected — false-positive prone with non-canonical YAML formatter

options.option_name: Status-field-only diff
options.description: Compare only the `status:` field; if equal, no-op.
pros: Simplest
cons: Misses transitions that add a companion field without changing status (e.g., back-filling adopted_by_feature_slug on an already-adopted file)
Misses FR-5 evolution case (escalated_to: addition with no status change on older file would be incorrectly no-op'd)
options.recommendation: rejected — too narrow; misses FR-5 and back-fill cases

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (frontmatter-state-diff). Correctly handles status transitions, companion-field back-fills, and the FR-5 transactional case; cheap to compute; matches the actual mutation surface.
risks: If D-05's per-state companion-field rules change between runs, an old file may diff against the new rule set — design-claude-code should specify that the proposed-frontmatter is computed against the LIVE D-05 rules, not the file's authoring-time rules

decisions.summary: Where does observability logging (write-path + user's selected option per AC-NFR-7-a) go — stderr only, project-relative file, both, or some other destination?
context_claims: PRD U-9 — defers to design-claude-code

PRD I-DR-004 note — test-acceptance-author should defer destination-specific assertions until U-9 closes

PRD §Won't Have — no UI surface, no notifications system

options.option_name: stderr + project-relative JSONL log at .claude/logs/capture-issue.jsonl
options.description: Every approved write emits two records: (a) one human-readable line to stderr (`capture-issue: wrote <path> (user selected: <option>)`); (b) one JSONL line appended to `.claude/logs/capture-issue.jsonl` with structured fields {ts, path, option, mode (create|update), topic_slug, doctype}. Matches log_state_transition.py's append-only JSONL pattern. Failure to append to JSONL falls back to stderr-only with a stderr warning (`capture-issue: log append failed: <reason>`).
pros: Matches sibling-script precedent (log_state_transition.py) — append-only JSONL is the established pattern
stderr line provides immediate session-tail visibility (AC-NFR-2-b's discipline)
JSONL log enables later analysis without re-running greps
Separates the log file from any pipeline working/ directory — outside-pipeline mechanism stores its observability OUTSIDE pipeline state (matches FR-13 isolation invariant)
Creating `.claude/logs/` is additive and zero-blast-radius
cons: Adds a new directory (`.claude/logs/`) to the project — small structural addition
JSONL append failure modes need design (filesystem-full, permissions); fail-open to stderr-only is the safe posture
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: stderr only
options.description: Single stderr line per approved write; no persistent log file.
pros: Zero file-creation; smallest footprint
cons: Loses post-hoc analyzability — stderr is session-scoped
Recipe-feature-pipeline §Won't Have lists only UI/notifications as excluded; persistent observability is not excluded
Lower fidelity than the sibling-script precedent (log_state_transition.py keeps a project-relative JSONL)
options.recommendation: rejected — loses post-hoc analyzability without proportional benefit

options.option_name: Project-relative JSONL only (no stderr)
options.description: Only JSONL log; no stderr line.
pros: Single destination; no duplication
cons: Silent in the active session — Josh would have no immediate confirmation the write succeeded beyond the AskUserQuestion result reporting (FR-1 AC-FR-1-c reports the path inline anyway, but that's the agent's report, not the observability record)
Failures to write to the JSONL go unnoticed without a stderr fallback
options.recommendation: rejected — no immediate session visibility on observability failures

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (stderr + project-relative JSONL). Matches log_state_transition.py precedent, provides both immediate and post-hoc visibility, fails open to stderr-only.
risks: Creating `.claude/logs/` is new — auditing-settings or auditing-cc-configs may flag the new directory; mitigated by additive documentation in .claude/SETTINGS-NOTES.md per FR-15
.gitignore semantics for `.claude/logs/capture-issue.jsonl` need a plan-stage decision (gitignore vs commit-as-audit-trail); recommend gitignore (logs are session-local)

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (fourth `issue` category branch inside validate_pipeline_artifact). Confirms F-012's recommendation. Single-validator, doc_type-keyed, mirrors GATED/ANALYSIS/ADR pattern, trivially backward-compatible.

decisions.summary: What is the concrete hook-latency threshold for AC-NFR-1-a (currently ~100ms target, deferred per U-11)?
context_claims: PRD U-11 — explicit deferral to design-claude-code once hook runtime (bash vs python vs other) is decided
PRD AC-NFR-1-a — '~100ms wall-clock per invocation on the standard devcontainer' is the PRD-time approximation
PRD AC-NFR-1-c — ratify or replace at design time
PRD NFR-1 — hook fires ~30-100 spawns/run; cumulative latency = N × per-spawn
D-02 recommends bash + jq (sub-100ms plausible)
kb.cc-platform-extensions — no documented benchmark in the KB for hook execution overhead
F-002 — no in-project baseline (first hook); design-time measurement must establish it

options.option_name: Confirm ~100ms per-invocation; measure at design time on the standard devcontainer; ratify if achieved
options.description: Process: (a) at design-claude-code Stage 5, run the bash + jq hook script (per D-02) 1000 times against synthetic stdin events; (b) measure 50th/95th/99th-percentile wall-clock; (c) if p95 ≤ 100ms, ratify AC-NFR-1-a unchanged; (d) if p95 > 100ms but ≤ 200ms, replace AC-NFR-1-a with the measured p95; (e) if p95 > 200ms, escalate to a design-iteration (revisit D-02 — possibly use a different language or pre-warmed daemon).
pros: Empirical; tied to actual implementation rather than guess
Symmetric thresholds (50th/95th/99th) match performance-test idiom
200ms ceiling matches user-perceptible-latency rule of thumb
Provides a clear escalation path back to D-02 if the implementation language fails
cons: Requires a measurement step at design time — small but real effort
Devcontainer baseline may not match GitHub Codespaces or other environments (only devcontainer is mentioned in AC-NFR-1-a — acceptable scope)
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Lower the threshold to 50ms
options.description: Tighten the target to 50ms p95.
pros: Stricter performance bar
cons: No baseline data supports 50ms as achievable for bash + jq
Tightening without measurement risks an unmet AC; better to measure first, then tighten if warranted
options.recommendation: rejected — speculative without baseline data

options.option_name: Remove the latency threshold; rely on AC-NFR-1-b only (no end-to-end regression)
options.description: Drop the per-invocation latency target; keep only the end-to-end no-regression test.
pros: No per-invocation measurement needed
cons: End-to-end regression may not catch a per-invocation latency that's individually tolerable but accumulates over 100 spawns
PRD I-DR-003 explicitly split the AC into measurable (1-a) + end-to-end (1-b) to address an earlier review finding; removing 1-a undoes that
options.recommendation: rejected — undoes deliberate PRD review-resolution

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (~100ms target, measure to ratify at design time). Provides empirical grounding and an escalation path back to D-02.
risks: If p95 > 200ms, the design-iteration triggers — D-02's option-2 (Python) and option-3 (Node) were rejected partly on this risk; if bash also fails, design-claude-code must propose a new option (pre-warmed daemon? compiled binary?)

ADR carries the architectural rationale; SETTINGS-NOTES carries the operational policy

decisions.summary: Should FR-8 migration of doc_type values (from {deferral-register, analysis, proposal} to {issue-register, issue-analysis, issue-proposal}) happen atomically with `git mv` or as a separate frontmatter back-fill commit?
context_claims: F-005 — doc_type naming inconsistency confirmed in all 4 pre-migration files
F-009 — pre-migration files at status:draft; migration back-fills status:open + since:
PRD AC-FR-8-a — paths to be migrated are enumerated
PRD AC-FR-8-b — `git log --follow` must return pre-migration history
PRD AC-FR-8-c — validator post-back-fill returns zero findings on migrated files
PRD AC-FR-9-a/b — agent-roster-impact-matrix.md migration via git mv with history preservation
blast_radius.touch_point[5] — referrers must update atomically or accept short-term stale references
known_issues[0] — FR-8 must back-fill values atomically
DISCOVERED-IN-FRAMING: not explicitly framed by any U-NN but implicit in the FR-8 procedure

options.option_name: Single atomic commit: `git mv` + frontmatter back-fill (doc_type rename + status:open + since: + version:0.1.0) in one commit
options.description: For each of the 4 Issues files + the agent-roster-impact-matrix file, a single commit performs: (a) `git mv` from flat path to per-issue folder path; (b) edit the moved file's frontmatter to change doc_type to the canonical enum, add status:open, add since: <derived-from-file-history>, add version:0.1.0. All 5 file-moves can be in one commit, or one commit per file — either way, each move is atomic with its back-fill. Cross-references in other documents (PRD, proposal, etc.) are updated in the same commit.
pros: git log --follow preserves history through the move-with-edit (git mv tracks history; the edit is a content change recorded on top of the rename)
Validator (post-FR-7) sees the migrated files in their final canonical state from commit 1 — no intermediate-state validation failures
No referrer-stale window: PRD/proposal references move from flat-path to folder-path in the same commit
Matches PRD §Dependencies posture (the migration is named as a one-time event)
cons: Larger single commit; harder to bisect if a back-fill turns out wrong

git mv + content-change in same commit is technically a heuristic move-detection by git (per blast_radius.touch_point[5] note) — but it works for content-changing moves at the default similarity-index
options.recommendation: recommended

options.option_name: Two-step: `git mv` first, then frontmatter back-fill in a follow-up commit
options.description: Commit 1: pure `git mv` (no content change). Commit 2: edit frontmatter on the moved files.
pros: Cleaner per-commit semantics (rename vs. content change separated)
Easier git bisect; smaller individual commits
cons: Between commits 1 and 2, the validator (running pre-merge) would see files with pre-migration doc_type values at their new paths — produces transient validation findings
Cross-reference updates in PRD/proposal would land in one of the two commits; the other would have stale references

PRD AC-FR-8-c expects validator-clean post-back-fill, but the staged approach means the back-fill commit is the validating commit and the rename commit alone is not validator-clean — adds ambiguity to the AC's measurement point
options.recommendation: rejected — introduces a transient invalid state that the AC framing does not anticipate

decisions.recommendation: Option 1 (single atomic commit per file or as a small commit-group). Preserves git log --follow, avoids transient invalid states, matches PRD AC-FR-8-c semantics.
risks: git's move-detection heuristic may classify a content-changing move as delete+add if the similarity falls below threshold — design-claude-code (FR-8 owner) should verify with a dry-run `git mv && edit && git diff -M` that detection holds; if not, fall back to a `git mv`-then-edit two-commit sequence ACKNOWLEDGED as an explicit risk-mitigation choice
FR-9's agent-roster-impact-matrix.md is a moved-but-not-renamed file (no doc_type change); single-atomic commit covers it trivially
